verification_note: Every url re-opened on 2026-10-03 (the kit's fetcher; the Byars site through WebFetch). All findings confirmed. Wording corrected: Griffen's circuit judgeship is in the Sixth Judicial District as the Encyclopedia words it, and the campaign About page cited beside the Encyclopedia was not re-checked, so those mentions were dropped from the source lines; Sylvester's page says he was elected in 2012 (the 2013 start is the January after); Rutledge's site is titled 'Leslie Rutledge for Lt. Governor' and paid for by that committee; Torres's site states the 2026 re-election as State Representative but does not print the district number.
note: The session's shared web-search allowance ran out after the first few searches of this part, so the rest was read directly: campaign sites, county and city pages, and a nonpartisan guide's district pages used only to find campaign addresses (each site was then opened and checked to name the candidate and the office). Ballotpedia answered the kit's fetcher with an empty page. No campaign site was found for Ryan Intchauspe, Cody Rogers, Dwight Tosh, Lee Johnson, Mark W. Perry, Sonia E. Barker, Justin Boyd, Cheesa Williams, Joy Kinman, Tony Stanley Miller, Todd Hoover, Ashley Brodnax or Richard Duncan. Checked and not holding the office sought: Cheesa Williams (not on Jacksonville's council directory), Tony Stanley Miller (not on Little Rock's Board of Directors page), Todd Hoover (Maumelle's council page lists Chad Gardner in Ward 2 Position 2). Sherwood's and Springdale's council pages could not be read. The Gazaway and Vaught campaign sites carry older content (a 2023 session newsletter; a 2022 copyright) but name the candidate, the district and the office.
